items.title: Opening "My orders" from the user menu shows the page heading "My orders"
items.reason: The bug is that the page header says "Orders" while the user-menu link says "My orders"; this case repeats the ticket's exact reproduction path (user menu, not a direct URL) and checks the heading text. It must be e2e because the heading is rendered by the WebApp layout's `page-header-title` section outlet and only exists in the browser.

items.title: The orders page's browser tab title is "My orders | AdventureWorks"
covers: Expected: tab title is "My orders | AdventureWorks"
items.reason: The second half of the bug is the document title ("Orders | AdventureWorks"); it is set by `PageTitle` and is a separate observable from the heading, so it gets its own case. Only a browser exposes `document.title`, so the layer is e2e.

items.title: The footer link "My orders" opens a page headed "My orders"
covers: Bug Report: footer link "My orders" matches the page it opens
items.reason: The bug report names two entry points, the user menu and the footer; this case proves the footer link and the destination's heading and title now agree. Separate from TC-PRB-2-01 because the footer is a different link in a different layout component (`FooterBar.razor`).

items.title: With no orders, the page body still shows the "No orders yet" empty state
covers: Expected: everything else on the page is unchanged (no-orders state)
items.reason: The ticket requires that only the heading and title change. alice has no orders in the `default` scenario, so the page body she sees is the empty state; this case guards against the text change disturbing it. e2e because the empty state is rendered markup.

items.title: With one order, the orders list still shows its header row and the order under the "My orders" heading
covers: Expected: the list of orders is unchanged
items.reason: The ticket states explicitly that "the list of orders" is unchanged. The `default` scenario has no orders, so the order is created through the WebApp checkout (the same path `e2e/CheckoutTest.spec.ts` uses) to make the list render. e2e because the list is WebApp markup fed by the Ordering API.

items.title: An anonymous visitor opening /user/orders is sent to the Login page and does not see the "My orders" page
covers: Expected: everything else on the page is unchanged (sign-in requirement of /user/orders)
items.reason: The ticket requires that everything on the orders page other than the heading and tab title is unchanged, and the page is only reachable signed in (the story's own steps start with "Sign in as alice"). Editing the page's top lines (`PageTitle` and the header section) sits right next to the page's `[Authorize]` attribute; if the sign-in requirement were lost, anyone could open another shopper's orders page. e2e because the redirect to the Identity login page only happens through the WebApp in a browser.
